newsitem.title: USA: CBS to launch Eye on People cable network.
newsitem.headline: CBS to launch Eye on People cable network.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS Cable will launch the CBS Eye on People cable network on March 31, CBS officials said on Wednesday.

The basic cable, advertiser-supported 24-hour network will offer entertainment and information programming that will capitalize on prominent CBS network personalities and on the promotional capacity of CBS television and radio affiliates, CBS Cable executives said at a press conference.
Lloyd Werner, executive vice president of sales and marketing at CBS Cable, said the network will be available in two million homes on Monday.
The network will be in three million homes by the end of April and should have 10 million subscribers by the end of 1997, he said.

Noting that Time Warner Inc cable systems will add 12 channels this year, Werner said CBS Eye on People is "under consideration" for one of those slots and CBS has been "led to believe that it's something they want."
Werner said CBS Eye on People plans to announce next week the names of advertisers it has signed.
Geoffrey Darby, president of CBS Eye on People, said it would take five or six years for the new CBS cable network to stop losing money and 10 to 12 years "to get all your money back with interest."
CBS Cable, formerly Group W Satellite Communications, is a division of Westinghouse Electric Corp's Westinghouse/CBS.

Werner said that because this is a "very difficult time" in the cable industry, cable operators are taking "a wait and see attitude" toward new networks. But he called CBS Eye on People "better than anything cable has produced in a decade."

Several of the cable network's new series will capitalize on CBS News' decades of journalistic efforts, offering viewers a behind-the-scenes look at the work. "60 Minutes More," anchored by CBS correspondent Mike Wallace, will revisit and update segments from the "60 Minutes" magazine broadcast with "60 Minutes" executive producer Don Hewitt offering his comments. Anchorwoman Paula Zahn will catch up with people who have stepped back from the public limelight on "Fast Forward."
Correspondent Charles Kuralt will anchor "I Remember," a series of first-person accounts by CBS News correspondents of events they covered.
The initial broadcast will look at the fall of Saigon through the eyes of CBS News correspondents Ed Bradley and Bob Simon, who were there.
Werner also said that "As more and more networks are transmogrifying into things they didn't promise to be, cable operators are writing strict (programming) guidelines."
CBS Eye on People "is not a news channel," Werner said.
(( -- Ellen Freilich, New York Wall Street Desk 212-859-1701))
